newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says 200 deserters back after amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says 200 deserters back after amnesty.

text.p: Sri Lanka, which this month announced a crackdown on army deserters promptly followed by an amnesty, said on Monday more than 200 of some 10,000 missing soldiers had returned to barracks.
The Ministry of Defence said the men had reported back to their regiments for duty and called on others to join them before the amnesty expires at midnight on July 21.

The government announced a general pardon for deserters on July 10, saying it was responding to appeals by parents who had asked that their children be forgiven for fleeing their posts on the battlefront.
The Sri Lankan army has been fighting the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) separatists since 1983.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
In a separate statement on Monday, the ministry said a policeman and civilian were killed on Sunday during a mortar attack by guerrillas on a police post in eastern Sri Lanka.
It also said naval patrols fought skirmishes with LTTE rebels off the north-eastern coast, destroying two LTTE boats.
